candidates.name: Show, Don't Just Tell, the Quote
candidates.mechanism: A static PDF or paper quote gets skimmed once and forgotten. A short personal video walking through the work and the price re-humanizes an otherwise generic document and keeps the customer engaged with it longer.
candidates.evidence: Proposify's State of Proposals research, reported by Vidyard, found proposals that included video closed at up to 41% higher rates, closed 26% faster, and drove 56% higher engagement than proposals without video.
candidates.transferTemplate: Instead of texting or emailing a flat PDF quote, send a short (2-3 minute) personal video alongside it: the technician standing at the job site explaining what's being fixed, why it costs what it costs, and what happens next. It turns a document the customer has to interpret alone into something that feels like the visit continuing after you've left.

candidates.name: Three Options, One Obvious Middle
candidates.mechanism: A middle option flanked by a bare-bones option and a premium option makes the middle choice feel like the safe, obviously reasonable pick. A single take-it-or-leave-it price instead invites a yes/no decision, which makes 'let me think about it' or 'let me shop around' the easy default.
candidates.evidence: When The Economist added a print-only subscription priced the same as its print+web bundle, alongside a cheaper web-only option, the added 'decoy' option shifted the mix toward the bundle and overall subscription sales rose by about 43%, according to the widely cited account of this pricing test.
candidates.transferTemplate: Instead of one number on the quote, offer three tiers — e.g. 'basic repair,' 'repair + tune-up,' and 'full replacement.' Price the middle option so it's clearly the practical choice next to the other two: most customers won't pick the cheapest or the priciest, they'll pick the one that feels like the safe middle, and the quote stops being a plain yes/no decision.

candidates.name: This Price Holds for 7 Days
candidates.mechanism: A decision with no deadline gets deferred indefinitely. A clear, real deadline on an offer forces the decision to happen at the point of maximum interest, instead of drifting until the customer forgets or moves on.
candidates.evidence: An e-commerce case study for pet supply retailer Bob & Lush found that adding a genuine urgency message to product pages (free next-day delivery if ordered by 4pm) produced a 27.1% revenue uplift and a 9.5% increase in checkout visits, measured over a 42-day test at 95% confidence.
candidates.transferTemplate: Put a real, honest deadline on the quote itself — 'this price is valid through [date] because material costs are re-quoted weekly' or 'this install slot is held for 48 hours.' The deadline has to be true, not a fake countdown, but a genuine one gives the customer a reason to decide now instead of letting 'I'll think about it' turn into never.
